verified_signals.signal: FY2025 annual operating report discloses the self-service fleet: on average 680,000 customers/month used the RSD cash-withdrawal function across 434 devices, of which 375 dispense RSD; almost 21 million ATM cash-withdrawal transactions in 2025 including 442,000 in EUR. (Verbatim: 'U proseku 680k klijenata mesecno koristio ovu funkcionalnost na 434 uredaja (od kojih 375 omogucava isplatu u RSD)'.) NOTE: the report does NOT say whether the 434 includes the 122 externally-sited ATMs owned by Payten under the 2023 outsourcing deal, so 434 may be a service-footprint count rather than a bank-owned asset count.
verified_signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (narrative annual report bound inside the audited separate financial statements PDF)
verified_signals.implies: First primary-source fleet count since the 2024-vintage data. 434 devices with only 375 RSD-dispensing implies ~59 units that are EUR-only or deposit-only - a functional gap Printec can address with multi-currency recyclers plus managed services.
verified_signals.likelihood: Fleet refresh continues; contract-driven replacement already underway (14 added + 26 replaced in 2025)
verified_signals.followup: Establish the basis of the 434 count - does it include the 122 Payten-owned external ATMs? Reconcile against the 2024-vintage 407 ATMs / 110 cash-in / 118 kiosks baseline, which this run could NOT independently source.

verified_signals.signal: FY2025 report: 123 multifunctional cash-in/cash-out self-service devices installed over the last five years (RSD deposit/withdrawal plus EUR transactions from FX payment accounts). RSD deposits at devices now 86% of the equivalent teller deposits (~120,000 customers/month); 73% of EUR deposits are device-migrated (~30,000 customers/month). 2025 volumes: 1.5m RSD deposits (+13.8%) worth almost RSD 56bn (+21.4%), and 386,000 EUR deposits (+18.6%) worth almost EUR 360m (+21.4%). ('Cash recycling' = an ATM that re-dispenses notes customers have deposited, cutting cash-replenishment trips.)
verified_signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (narrative annual report bound inside the audited separate financial statements PDF)
verified_signals.implies: A proven, quantified recycler business case at the #1 Serbian bank - direct fit for Printec cash automation/recyclers and cash-cycle managed services; only 123 of 434 devices are multifunctional, so roughly 70% of the estate is still cash-out only.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - migration rates already at 86%/73% and the report frames the network as continuing to expand
verified_signals.followup: Identify the OEM of the 123 multifunctional units and the replacement cadence. Diebold Nixdorf Cineo is a reasonable inference from the Payten releases of 04/03/2020 and 13/12/2023 but is NOT stated anywhere for the 2025 estate.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Verified verbatim in my own extraction of the FS PDF: 'Instalirano je ukupno 123 multifunkcionalnih uredaja'; '...ove transakcije sada cine cak 86% svih uplata u odnosu na iste transakcije obavljene na salterima'; 'Uplatu u evrima koristi u proseku 30k klijenata na mesecnom nivou (73% EUR uplata se izvrse na uredajima)'; '1,5 miliona uplata u RSD, sto je 13,8% vise... skoro 56 milijardi RSD (+21,4%). 386 hiljada uplata u EUR... 18,6%... skoro 360 miliona EUR (+21,4%)'. verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2023] CORRECTION to baseline: the '200 ATMs replaced with Diebold Nixdorf Cineo incl. recycling' story is a Payten release dated 04/03/2020, NOT part of the 2023 outsourcing. The 13/12/2023 page confirms verbatim: '122 ATM machines situated in Banca Intesa external locations', '36 months', 'In the first 12 months of the contract Payten shall replace all existing installed ATM machines with latest generation Diebold-Nixdorf CashOut and Recycling devices', 'security upgrades with Vynamic Security suite software', 'eliminated all mandate risks related to VISA, MC, PCI DSS', plus lease-contract responsibility. The 2020 release (the researcher's URL was wrong - the working URL is https://www.payten.com/en/news-events/news/banca-intesa-strengthens-its-atm-network-supported-payten/ , without 'by') is confirmed dated 04 MAR 2020 and does say 'replacement of 200 ATMs' with 'new Diebold Nixdorf Cineo ATMs' and 'A portion of new units will come equipped with recycling possibilities'. TWO CORRECTIONS I MADE: (1) is_new set to false and the signal tagged [STANDING - dated 2023] - the underlying event is 2.6 years old and the only forward trigger is an inferred expiry; (2) opp_size cut XL to L - no contract value is disclosed by either party, and 122 devices is ~28% of the 434-device estate, so neither the '>=EUR 5m' nor the 'footprint-wide' test for XL is supported by evidence.

verified_signals.signal: CORRECTED: the FY2025 audited note on right-of-use assets states that for leases of POS terminals and accompanying devices, and of ATM and ATS printer units, the bank applied a portfolio approach on initial recognition. It does NOT say the whole ATM estate is leased. The wider lease note lists the recognised right-of-use classes as real estate, cars, IT equipment (two server leases) and other equipment; total right-of-use gross carrying amount rose from RSD 4,454,283k (01/01/2024) to RSD 5,217,268k (31/12/2024), with RSD 670,466k of additions in 2025 - and equipment is NOT broken out separately from property in the disclosed table.
verified_signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Napomene uz pojedinacne finansijske izvestaje za 2025, Note 20(a) Sredstva sa pravom koriscenja
verified_signals.implies: The bank does use lease/opex structures for at least part of its POS and self-service device estate, so Printec should be ready to bid opex/managed-service commercial models rather than capex sales. But the note does NOT establish that ATMs as a whole are off-balance-sheet, and it cannot be used to size annual device spend.
verified_signals.likelihood: Structural; relevant to any future bid
verified_signals.followup: Ask the bank (or infer from a future note) what share of the RSD 5.2bn right-of-use balance is device equipment vs real estate - the disclosed table merges them, so the annual device spend is NOT derivable from the published accounts.
verified_signals.verifier_note: The quoted sentence is real, verbatim: 'Po osnovu ugovora o zakupu POS terminala i pratecih uredaja, ATM i ATS uredjaja stampaca, Banka je prilikom priznavanja sredstva sa pravom koriscenja koristila portfolio pristup.' BUT the researcher's implication over-reads it. Read literally the leased items are POS terminals + accompanying devices + ATM/ATS PRINTER units - the Serbian ('ATM i ATS uredjaja stampaca') most plausibly attaches 'stampaca' (printers) to the ATM/ATS devices. Separately, accounting-policy note 2.17 lists the right-of-use classes as 'zakup nepokretnosti, automobila, ICT opreme i ostale opreme' - real estate, cars, ICT and other equipment - with no ATM-fleet class. And the 122 external ATMs are OWNED BY PAYTEN under the outsourcing deal, not leased by the bank, which is a different structure again. I therefore rewrote the signal to what the source actually supports, cut opp_size L to M, and killed the researcher's followup ('extract the RSD value of equipment right-of-use assets') because I checked the Note 20 table and equipment is not separated from property there.

verified_signals.signal: FY2025 strategy section (chapter 5, pillar III 'Poboljsanje okvira rizika/kontrole i upravljanje') commits to strengthening governance and internal controls 'kroz unapredeno upravljanje nefinansijskim rizicima i digitalizaciju procesa u oblasti sprecavanja finansijskog kriminala i uskladenosti' - i.e. digitalising financial-crime-prevention and compliance processes - explicitly to improve oversight and reduce operational losses. AML is embedded as a Risk Appetite Framework measure, and in 2025 a new set of RAF indicators (monitored but not limit-bound) was introduced specifically to manage AML risk, legal risk and IT risk. 2,611 employees took anti-bribery and AML training totalling 23,130 hours; an AML Akademija runs internally.

verified_signals.implies: An explicit, board-level programme to digitalise financial-crime prevention - direct fit for Printec AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring, and the clearest stated software need in the whole report. No budget figure is disclosed.
verified_signals.followup: Establish whether the AML/transaction-monitoring platform is an Intesa Sanpaolo group mandate or a local buy - decisive for whether Printec can bid at all. Note operational-risk methodology is already explicitly 'u skladu sa metodologijom Maticne banke'.
verified_signals.verifier_note: All three elements verified in my own text extraction. Strategy quote confirmed verbatim. RAF wording confirmed verbatim: 'Indikatori kapaciteta resolvabilnosti, stabilnosti profita, trzisne i makroekonomske stabilnosti, kvaliteta aktive, nefinansijskog rizika i AML predstavljaju dodatne RAF mere. U 2025. godini uvedeni su novi limiti medu indikatorima ranog upozorenja... kao i set RAF indikatora koji se prate a nisu predmet RAF limita ili praga ranog upozorenje u cilju upravljanja AML rizikom, pravnim rizikom i IT rizikom.' verified_signals.signal: CORRECTED AND UPGRADED TO PRIMARY: on 04/06/2026 the NBS published for public consultation (comments due 11/06/2026, now closed) a Draft of amendments to the Law on Interbank Fees and Special Rules for Card-Based Payment Transactions which for the first time caps interchange on cards issued OUTSIDE Serbia when used at a Serbian acquirer. The draft Article 3 sets FOUR new caps, not two: card-present foreign debit 0.2% and foreign credit 0.3% (matching the domestic caps already in the law, Official Gazette RS 44/2018), but card-NOT-present (e-commerce) foreign debit 1.15% and foreign credit 1.5%. NBS states the aim is to improve transparency and lower merchants' card-acceptance costs in line with EU practice.
verified_signals.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije, Nacrt izmena i dopuna Zakona o medubankarskim naknadama i posebnim pravilima poslovanja kod platnih transakcija na osnovu platnih kartica (public-consultation drafts register)
verified_signals.implies: Compresses acquiring economics on the fast-growing foreign-tourist card volume (foreign-card payments +18.6% YoY per NBS), pushing acquirers toward volume and lower cost-to-serve - favours Printec POS estate managed services and terminal-fleet efficiency plays over margin-funded hardware. The much higher CNP caps mean the squeeze lands mainly on physical POS, i.e. exactly the estate Printec serves.
verified_signals.likelihood: Consultation closed 11/06/2026; adoption plausible but no parliamentary timetable is published
verified_signals.followup: Track the draft's progress to the Serbian parliament and watch for the transitional application date - the draft text sets the caps but this run found no published entry-into-force date.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I LOCATED THE PRIMARY SOURCE the researcher could not find, which closes operator request #2. Route: nbs.rs /sr/drugi-nivo-navigacije/propisi/nacrti/ -> the draft PDF. Extracted with pdfminer. THREE MATERIAL CORRECTIONS to the researcher's version: (1) DATE - the draft was published 04/06/2026 with a consultation deadline of 11/06/2026, not '16/06/2026'; the researcher's date came from N1 coverage, and even that article is dated 14/06/2026, not 16/06. (2) SCOPE - the draft does NOT apply a flat 0.2%/0.3% to all foreign cards. Article 3 as amended reads (capitals are the draft's insertions): card-PRESENT foreign debit 'НЕ МОЖЕ БИТИ ВИША ОД 0,2%', card-present foreign credit '0,3%', card-NOT-present foreign debit '1,15%', card-not-present foreign credit '1,5%'. Presenting this as a uniform 0.2/0.3 cap on foreign cards would materially misstate the economics. (3) SOURCE TIER - upgraded press to regulator primary, so confidence goes Low to Medium. I also confirmed the domestic 0.2/0.3 caps sit in the existing law published in Official Gazette RS 44/2018. opp_size M cut to Unscoped: this is a regulatory/macro driver, not a scoped account opportunity.

verified_signals.signal: CORRECTED: on the ASEE Q2/H1-2026 earnings call held 27/07/2026, CEO Piotr Jelenski said of the ATM business: 'If we had hardware on our balance sheet, we were financing it with debt. Not all of it. Now we will finance all of the outsourced things with debt', and 'We will be more disciplined... we want to offload the capital deployment or kind of pressure on capital utilization unnecessary on us', adding 'Can I imagine there will be no hardware on our balance sheet? Of course, I can imagine'. ASEE's FY2023 management report separately records that in the ATM business line 'weaker revenues were recorded mainly by our operations in Serbia', caused by lower hardware deliveries and only partly offset by growth in own maintenance services, and that group capex is 'mostly financed from the Group's own funds, except for infrastructure used in the outsourcing of payment processes that is largely financed with bank loans'.
verified_signals.source_name: Investing.com transcript of the ASEE Q2/H1-2026 earnings call (27/07/2026); ASEE Group Management Report for the year ended 31 December 2023
verified_signals.implies: CAUTION - this is a change in how the incumbent FINANCES ATM-as-a-service (debt rather than own funds), not a retreat from it; if anything it signals intent to keep growing outsourcing while protecting capital. The genuinely useful read for Printec is that ASEE is capital-constrained on this line and openly contemplating zero hardware on its balance sheet, which could change the shape of any Banca Intesa renewal offer. Treat as a competitor-posture driver, not a scoped opportunity.
verified_signals.likelihood: Financing-policy statement is on the record; any effect on the Banca Intesa renewal is unproven speculation
verified_signals.followup: Obtain the ASEE FY2025 management report and the primary H1-2026 report from asee.io investor relations (asee.io/investor-relations/periodic-reports/ returned 404 for me too) for ATM-outsourcing capex and Serbian contract-pipeline commentary.

verified_signals.verifier_note: Verified verbatim: 'Razvoj PD, LGD i EAD modela podeljen je u tri faze, a celokupan razvoj sproveden je na novoj platformi koriscenjem BigQuery i Vertex AI servisa na Google Cloud-u. Svi algoritmi korisceni u modeliranju implementirani su u Python-u... uskladeni sa lokalnim i ECB regulatornim zahtevima.' The milestone dates ('Validacija i implementacija modela planirane su za prvu polovinu 2026. godine'; 'finalizacija razvoja modela planirana je za drugi kvartal 2026'; 'Rekonstrukcija podataka o defaultu za pravna lica bice nastavljena u prvom kvartalu 2026') all check out. Jargon note for the brief: PD/LGD/EAD are the probability of default, loss given default and exposure at default parameters banks use to size credit risk capital.
